name: Process returned debits and cheques
summary: About 85% of customers pay their lease by pre-authorised debit, and each month around 1,300 debits and cheques come back unpaid, mostly for insufficient funds and the rest for closed accounts, stopped payments or claims. A cash application clerk downloads the bank's returns report each morning, matches each item to its contract, reverses the payment in the lease system, adds the returned payment fee and places the account in the early collections queue, while a billing specialist checks the few returns that point to a company error. The work is short per item but must be done the same day so collectors can re-present the debit within the 30 days Payments Canada allows, and it goes wrong when returns cannot be matched, debit holds are missed or a customer is chased for a debit the company should not have sent.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size Canadian independent equipment lessor with about 55,000 active contracts, a lease management system with daily batch billing and reversal, a bank cash management portal and a separate collections queue.
baseline.notes: Returns arrive as a daily report and file from the clearing bank. Reversals are keyed into a batch the lease system processes overnight. Re-presentment of NSF debits is done by early-stage collectors and is not part of this process.

trigger: The clearing bank reports a pre-authorised debit returned by the customer's bank, or a cheque returned unpaid after apply-customer-payments posted it.
end_state: The payment is reversed, the fee is billed and the account sits in the early collections queue with its return reason, or a company debit error is corrected with no fee and no collection action.

volume.seasonality: Returns cluster on the first business days of the month, when most lease debits fall due, and rose in spring 2020 when many small businesses lost revenue before deferrals were agreed.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's process map: about 2.5% of roughly 47,000 monthly debits return in a normal month, with the high end for 2020.

roles.title: Cash application and payment processing clerk

evidence.note: Wage basis from Job Bank NOC 14200, loaded as in the organisation file (wage times 1.35, about 90% of 2023-2024 levels). FTE is a tier C estimate. The steps imply about 9 to 10 minutes of clerk time per return, or about 1.5 FTE at 1,300 returns a month, but the organisation file leaves only about 1.0 FTE of this role unclaimed, so 1.0 is stated and the gap is noted in the assumptions.
Investigates claims and possible debit errors (about 10% of returns) and corrects billing on company errors, about 2 to 3 minutes per return on average. Cost from the organisation file.
Daily sign-off of the returns reconciliation and approval of fee waivers. Cost from the organisation file.
Decides whether repeat returners come off automatic debit, about 12% of returns. Cost from the organisation file.

systems.name: Bank cash management portal for pre-authorised debit files, EFT payments and wires
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)
Document imaging and contract file store
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)

steps.name: Bank returns the dishonoured payment
steps.description: The customer's bank refuses the lease debit (insufficient funds, payment stopped, account closed or frozen, or a reimbursement claim) and sends it back through the clearing system to the company's clearing bank, which debits the company's account. A cheque returned unpaid comes back the same way as a chargeback with an image. Under Payments Canada rules the item must be returned by the business day after the payor's bank receives it.
outputs: returned item at the clearing bank

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Returned by the next business day (Rule H1 s.22) and reported to the originator usually one or two days after the due date (Central 1 guide). Weekends and holidays stretch the high end. Reimbursement claims can arrive up to 10 business days after the debit; they are a small share and are not modelled as a separate wait.

steps.name: Download the day's returns from the bank portal
steps.description: Each morning a cash application clerk logs into the bank's cash management portal, downloads the returned items report and return file for the previous day's debits and cheques, prints or saves it to the shared folder, and notes the item count and total so the day's reversals can be balanced later.
outputs: day's returns list with count and total

error.defect_description: An item on the report is missed when the list is copied.

evidence.note: The guide tells originators to check the returns report each business day. Touch is per item; the report run takes 10 to 20 minutes for the whole day's list.

steps.name: Match the return to its contract and debit
steps.description: For each item the clerk reads the cross-reference number and return code, opens the contract in the lease system and checks that the amount, due date and bank account match a debit in the file billing sent. Items with no usable reference, a consolidated debit covering several contracts or a paper cheque chargeback are set aside for research.

error.defect_description: Return matched to the wrong contract of the same customer.

next.condition: no match or several contracts in one debit

evidence.note: Search by account, date, amount or reference is the documented way to find the payment to reverse. Shares are tier C estimates; the cheque share follows apply-customer-payments, which sends about 90 returned cheques a month (1% of 9,000 items).

steps.name: Research a return that does not match
steps.description: The clerk looks for the contract behind an unclear return: searches the customer's other contracts, checks whether the contract number changed after a restructure, assumption or rebooking, and splits a consolidated debit across the contracts it paid. When the debit belongs to a contract already paid out, the clerk notes it as a possible debit error for billing to review.

error.defect_description: Consolidated debit split across contracts in the wrong amounts.

evidence.note: Based on the unmatched-item research described for cash application and on how lease systems store contract numbers.

steps.name: Pull the returned cheque and chargeback advice
steps.description: For a cheque that apply-customer-payments posted and the bank later returned unpaid, the clerk retrieves the cheque image and the bank's chargeback advice, notes the return reason and the payment it reversed, and checks whether the bank will redeposit it or a replacement payment must be requested.
outputs: returned cheque linked to the posted payment

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Returned cheques reach this process from apply-customer-payments; times are estimates.

steps.name: Key the reversal with its return reason
steps.description: The clerk adds the item to the day's payment reversal batch in the lease system with the contract, the original payment reference, the amount and the reason code (non-sufficient funds, stop payment, account closed, claim, other), so the payment comes off the invoice it paid and the invoice shows as unpaid again.

error.defect_description: Wrong reason code or amount keyed.

evidence.note: Lease systems take reversals with an NSF or stop payment reason code. Touch time is tier C.

steps.name: Run the overnight reversal update
steps.description: After the end-of-day cut-off the lease system processes the reversal batch: it reverses each payment, reapplies any later payments to the oldest open invoice, updates the contract's days past due and the collections data sent to treasury and funders, posts the reversal to the cash and receivable accounts, and prints an exception report and an audit report.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: The documented batch reversal runs as a daily end-of-period update with exception and audit reports. Wait covers the time from keying to the overnight run.

steps.name: Reconcile the day's returns to the bank and the ledger
steps.description: Next morning the clerk compares the count and total of returned items debited to the company's bank account with the reversal audit report and the general ledger cash entry, and works the exception report. Differences (a missed item, a reversal suspense line, a wrong amount) are listed for correction.

error.defect_description: A small difference is carried forward without being cleared.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: daily reconciliation of bank activity to the lease sub-ledger and the general ledger; accurate collections data for securitisation servicer reports

evidence.note: Exception and audit reports and the daily returns report are documented. The 5% exception share and times are tier C.

steps.name: Clear reversal exceptions and differences
steps.description: The clerk fixes what the overnight run could not do: reverses by hand a payment that was part of a multi-contract batch, clears a reversal suspense item, corrects a wrong amount or reason code, and adds any missed item to tonight's batch.

error.defect_description: Manual reversal applied to the wrong invoice.

evidence.note: Multi-lease batches are skipped by the documented batch reversal and need manual work. Times are tier C.

steps.name: Sign off the daily returns reconciliation
steps.description: The billing manager reviews the reconciliation sheet, the count and value of returns against recent days and any open differences, initials it, and asks for explanations of large or unusual returns, such as a whole dealer's customers returning on one day.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: reconciliations reviewed and approved by someone other than the preparer

evidence.note: Common control practice; touch is per item as the sign-off covers the whole day's list. In practice the follow-up work in s11 does not wait for the sign-off.

steps.name: Classify the return reason and choose the follow-up
steps.description: The clerk sorts each return by its code and the account notes: insufficient funds or funds not cleared go straight to the fee and collections steps; account closed, invalid account, no debit allowed or frozen need new banking details; payment stopped or customer-initiated returns need a look for a reason; reimbursement claims and returns that suggest the company debited wrongly go to billing.

error.defect_description: A debit error is treated as a customer default.

next.condition: insufficient funds or funds not cleared
account closed, invalid, frozen or no debit allowed
reimbursement claim or suspected debit error

evidence.note: Return codes and claim codes come from the bank guide and Rule H1. The split by reason is a tier C estimate for small business lease debits.

steps.name: Hold the debit and ask for new banking details
steps.description: For a closed, invalid or frozen account the clerk sets a debit hold on the contract so tomorrow's billing run does not send another debit that will fail, records the reason, and e-mails or mails the customer a new pre-authorised debit form asking for a void cheque for the new account. New details that arrive later are entered by billing or customer service.

error.defect_description: Debit hold not set, so the next debit fails again.

control.basis: Payments Canada Rule H1: debits may be drawn only on the account the payor authorised; a new account needs a new PAD agreement

evidence.note: The bank guide tells originators to obtain correct account information and update the record. Times are tier C.

steps.name: Look into a stopped payment
steps.description: The clerk reads the contract notes and recent contacts to see why the customer stopped the debit: a dispute over the equipment, a recent payout or buyout, a sale of the business, a switch of bank or a sign of closing. A stop placed after a payout or an agreed change is passed to billing as a possible debit error; the rest are flagged as priority for collections.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: stop after payout, deferral or agreed change

evidence.note: Based on the reasons customers stop debits on leases; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Investigate a claim or a possible debit error
steps.description: A billing specialist opens the signed PAD agreement in imaging, the billing history and any payout, deferral, restructure or banking change, and checks whether the debit followed the agreement: right amount, right date, pre-notification of a changed amount, and no debit after a payout or an agreed deferral. They decide whether the company debited in error or the customer simply refused a valid debit.
inputs: return with claim or error flag

error.defect_description: A valid debit is judged an error, or the reverse.

control.basis: Payments Canada Rule H1 sections 23 and 24: reimbursement claims for business PADs within 10 business days of the debit; pre-notification rules for changed amounts

evidence.note: Claim grounds and windows from Rule H1 and the Payments Canada guide. The error share and times are tier C.

steps.name: Add the returned payment fee
steps.description: The clerk keys the returned payment fee set out in the lease (commonly $25 to $50) as a miscellaneous charge on the contract so it bills on the next invoice, as a billing adjustment that billing checks in its daily run. The fee cannot be added to a re-presented debit, which must be for the same amount as the original.

error.defect_description: Fee missed or keyed on the wrong contract.

control.basis: Payments Canada Rule H1 s.22(c) and Payee Letter of Undertaking s.20: a re-presented PAD must be for the original amount without NSF charges, so fees are billed separately; fee amount per the lease agreement

evidence.note: Separate fee billing follows from Rule H1; lease systems assess the NSF fee with the reversal. The $25 to $50 fee level is a tier C estimate.

steps.name: Check the return history for repeat returns
steps.description: The clerk looks at the contract's payment history for earlier returned debits in the last twelve months. A customer with two or more earlier returns is referred to collections to decide whether to keep debiting.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Repeat-return review is common lessor practice; the 12% share is an estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether to take a repeat returner off debit
steps.description: An early-stage collector reviews the account and decides whether to keep the automatic debit, take the customer off debit and ask for payment by EFT or certified cheque until the account is current, or ask for a new debit date that matches the customer's cash flow.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Collections policy on repeated returned debits

evidence.note: Billing's debit file hold list includes accounts collections asked to take off debit after repeated returns (efc-bill-customers s10). Times and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Switch the contract to invoice payment and send the letter
steps.description: The clerk changes the payment method on the contract from debit to invoice, sets the hold so billing's debit file skips it, and sends the customer a letter with the amount due, the returned payment fee and how to pay by EFT, bill payment or certified cheque.

error.defect_description: Payment method changed but the debit hold missed, so one more debit is sent.

evidence.note: Estimate based on the debit hold practice in efc-bill-customers.

steps.name: Place the account in the early collections queue
steps.description: The clerk codes the returned payment in the collections system with the return code, the fee, flags for a stopped payment, a closed account or a repeat return, and a short note, so the account appears in an early-stage collector's queue with the right priority. Customers who have already called to arrange payment are noted so the collector does not chase them twice.
outputs: delinquent account in the collections queue

error.defect_description: Wrong flag or missing note, so the collector misses the reason for the return.

evidence.note: Returned payments go to collections work on delinquent leases. Times are tier C.

steps.name: Approve the fee waiver and billing correction
steps.description: The billing manager reviews the specialist's finding and approves the correction: no returned payment fee, reversal of any late charge, and a fix to the debit schedule or the payout record; corrections above the specialist's limit and any refund need this approval.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Delegated authority for fee waivers, credits and refunds

evidence.note: Approval limits for credits and waivers are common billing controls; times are estimates.

steps.name: Correct the billing and confirm with the customer
steps.description: The billing specialist keys the correction in the lease system, sends the billing adjustment for the next invoice, removes any collection flag, fixes the debit schedule or marks the contract closed, and e-mails or calls the customer to confirm what will be debited next and that no fee applies.

error.defect_description: Correction keyed on the wrong invoice.

evidence.note: Estimate based on the adjustment work described in efc-bill-customers.

exceptions.name: Return that cannot be matched
exceptions.description: No usable reference, a consolidated debit for several contracts or a contract renumbered after a restructure; the clerk researches before reversing.

exceptions.name: Returned cheque
exceptions.description: A cheque posted by cash application is returned unpaid as a chargeback and has to be linked back to the payment it reversed.

exceptions.name: Reversal exception or reconciliation difference
exceptions.description: The overnight run skips a multi-contract batch or creates a suspense item, or the returns do not balance to the bank.

exceptions.name: Closed or invalid account
exceptions.description: The debit hold is set and the customer is asked for a new PAD form before the next debit date.

exceptions.name: Company debit error
exceptions.description: A debit sent after a payout or an agreed deferral, a wrong amount without pre-notification, or a duplicate; no fee and no collection action.

exceptions.name: Repeat returner
exceptions.description: A collector decides whether to take the customer off debit; half are switched to invoice payment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the debit due date to the account in the collections queue or the error corrected
benchmarks.population: Canadian PAD originators; lessor practice of same-day processing of the returns report

evidence.note: Returns come back by the next business day and are reported usually one or two days after the due date; the organisation file says the clerk places the account in collections the same day the return is processed. Adding the overnight reversal run and weekends gives about 2 to 3 days at the median.

benchmarks.unit: re-presentments of an NSF or funds-not-cleared debit
days after the debit due date
benchmarks.population: AFT originators using a credit union central's file service

benchmarks.unit: past due interest charged by one Canadian bank-owned equipment lessor

benchmarks.population: This organisation in a normal month

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate; no published Canadian lessor figure was found.

pain_points.description: The 30-day window for the single re-presentment starts on the original debit date, so every day a return waits for reversal and queue placement shortens the time collectors have to reach the customer and re-debit.

evidence.note: Window from Rule H1; the effect on collections is the author's reading.

pain_points.description: Returns with no usable reference, consolidated debits and renumbered contracts need research, and batch reversal skips multi-contract batches, leaving manual reversals and suspense items.
When a debit hold or payment method change is missed, the next billing run sends another debit to a closed account, creating a second return and a second fee the customer disputes.

evidence.note: Common failure noted in billing hold lists; frequency is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Debits sent after a payout, an agreed deferral or a changed amount without notice produce claims, fee waivers and complaints, and the account is sometimes chased before billing has found the company's error.

evidence.note: Claim grounds from Rule H1; the chasing problem is tier C.

pain_points.description: Returns peak on the first business days of the month and rose sharply in 2020, while the same clerks also run cash application, so returns compete with unapplied cash for the morning.

evidence.note: Debit dates concentrate at month start; 2020 rise per the organisation file.

sources.title: Rule H1 Pre-Authorized Debits (PADs)
sources.supports: Section 22: a dishonoured PAD (NSF, stop payment, account closed) must be returned no later than the business day after receipt; a dishonoured PAD may be re-presented only for the same amount, without additional charges. Section 24: a business PAD reimbursement claim may be made up to 10 business days after the debit. Appendix (Payee Letter of Undertaking) section 20: after an NSF or funds-not-cleared return the payee may re-present once, within 30 calendar days, with no interest or NSF charges. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

sources.title: Pre-authorized debit (business guide)
sources.supports: If the payor's bank cannot pay, the PAD comes back by the next business day; one re-presentment within 30 days for the exact same amount and without the payee's fees; an NSF payment does not cancel the PAD agreement; business PAD claims within 10 days; the payee's institution notifies it of returned PADs.

sources.title: PaymentStream AFT Guide for File Upload
sources.publisher: Central 1 Credit Union (published by Prospera Credit Union)
sources.supports: Returned AFT transactions appear on the consolidated returns, recalls, rejects and error corrections report, usually one or two days after the due date; return codes 901 NSF, 902 account not found, 903 payment stopped, 905 account closed, 907 no debit allowed, 908 funds not cleared, 911 account frozen, 912 invalid account number, 915 to 921 reimbursement claims, 922 customer initiated return; the originator checks the report each business day, investigates the reason, obtains correct account information and arranges payment of the returned item. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

sources.title: U0470 Batch Payment Reversal
sources.supports: A lease system's daily end-of-period update reverses payments listed in an input file with a reason code (N non-sufficient funds, S stop payment), reverses and reapplies later payments by due date, skips batches that span several leases, creates reversal suspense items when lines do not match, and prints an exception report and an audit report.

sources.title: Reversing payment transaction and assessing NSF fee (Lending and Leasing user guide 15.0)
sources.supports: In a lending and leasing servicing system the user searches posted payments by account, date, amount or reference, selects the payment and clicks NSF; the system reverses the original payment and assesses the NSF fee.

sources.title: Equipment financing: lease payments and invoices
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment lessor charges past due interest at 2% a month with a minimum of $10 when a payment is made after its due date, charges $5 to generate an invoice unless the customer pays by pre-authorised debit, and may require pre-authorised debit as a condition of credit approval.

sources.title: Equipment Leasing Account Specialist (job posting)
sources.supports: An equipment finance company's account specialist manages existing leases in the portfolio for returned payments, contacts customers to resolve missed or delinquent payments and resolves disputes about balances due.

sources.title: Collections FAQs (Customer Connect help center)
sources.supports: A lease servicer's past-due timeline: a late fee accrues on day 1, a letter and e-mail go out on days 5 to 7, calls and e-mails follow to day 28, and collection efforts escalate on day 31; insufficient funds can send an account to collections before the first bill.

sources.title: Wages for accounting and related clerks (NOC 14200)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $18.12, median $25.00, high $37.00 (2023-2024).

assumptions: Volume and the 85% debit share come from the organisation file. The split of return reasons (66% insufficient funds or funds not cleared, 14% closed or invalid accounts, 12% stopped or customer-initiated, 8% claims and suspected company errors) is the author's estimate; no Canadian lessor breakdown was found.

The organisation file says the clerk places the account in collections the same day. In this model reversals post in an overnight batch, so the queue placement usually completes the morning after the return is downloaded; the account is already visible as returned in the lease system on the first day.

Re-presentment of NSF debits, collection notices and calls belong to collect-early-stage; entering new banking details when they arrive belongs to billing or customer service. Neither is modelled here.
Returned cheques (about 7% of cases) come from apply-customer-payments, which ends about 1% of its 9,000 items as returned cheques.

collect-early-stage states that 75% of its 2,700 monthly accounts come from this process (about 2,000), but this process sends only about 1,250 a month at the process map's mode of 1,300 returns. The two figures in the organisation file and the existing workflow do not agree; this file keeps the process map volume.

Clerk time is about 5 to 6 minutes per return on the common path and 9 to 10 minutes on average once research, exceptions and letters are included, about 1.5 FTE at 1,300 returns a month. Only about 1.0 FTE of cash application clerk time is left unclaimed in the organisation file (7 clerks, 6.0 FTE already claimed), so the role is stated at 1.0 FTE and the organisation file looks about half a clerk short; at the 2020 peak of 2,400 returns the work would need nearly 3 clerks, which the model assumes came from overtime and borrowed billing staff.
The returned payment fee of $25 to $50 is an estimate of common lease terms; the model does not depend on the amount.
Loaded hourly costs are the organisation file's (wage times 1.35).
